lesson.title: Defining Functions
intro: A **function** is a relation in which each input has exactly **one** output.
You can test a relation by checking ordered pairs, tables, mappings, and graphs. If one input is paired with two different outputs, the relation is **not** a function.
On graphs, use the **vertical line test**: if any vertical line hits the graph more than once, the graph does not represent a function.

questions.prompt: Three relations are shown below. Which relations represent a function?
questions.explanation: All three relations are functions. In I, each x-value appears once. In II, each input points to exactly one output. In III, every x-value on the graph has only one y-value.

questions.prompt: Which of the graphs represent(s) a function?
questions.explanation: Graphs A and B are functions because each x-value gives only one y-value. Graph C fails the vertical line test because of the vertical line, and graph D fails because a circle gives two y-values for many x-values.

questions.prompt: Given the relation **R = {(-1,1),(0,3),(-2,-4),(x,5)}**, which value of **x** will make the relation a function?
questions.explanation: To be a function, no input can repeat with a different output. The existing x-values are -1, 0, and -2, so choosing 4 keeps all inputs unique.

questions.prompt: The table below represents a relation. What value of **x** would make the relation a function?
questions.explanation: A function cannot repeat an input with a different output. Choosing 3 keeps all x-values unique.
